title: Flamingos Aren't Born Pink

scenes.narration: Flamingos are not born pink. Their chicks hatch fluffy and grey.
scenes.image_prompt: a fluffy grey flamingo chick standing in shallow water beside its pink parent, soft morning light

scenes.narration: The pink comes from their food: algae and tiny brine shrimp packed with carotenoids, the same pigments that make carrots orange.
scenes.image_prompt: a pink flamingo filter feeding in a shallow salt lake full of orange algae, reflections on the water

scenes.narration: Their liver turns those pigments into pink and orange molecules and stores them in their feathers, skin and legs.
scenes.image_prompt: extreme close-up of vivid pink and coral flamingo feathers, fine detail

scenes.narration: Zoos add these pigments to their food. Without them, new feathers grow in pale.
scenes.image_prompt: a flock of pale pink flamingos standing in a green zoo pond

scenes.narration: In mating season they rub pigment-rich oil from a gland near the tail onto their feathers. Flamingo makeup!
scenes.image_prompt: a bright pink flamingo preening its feathers with its beak at golden hour

scenes.narration: The pinkest birds tend to find mates first. Follow for more.
scenes.image_prompt: a huge flock of pink flamingos wading at sunset, warm orange sky

description: Flamingos hatch grey. Their colour comes from carotenoid pigments in algae and brine shrimp, and they even top it up with a kind of natural makeup in mating season.
